correctness.rationale: For each long branch, the cotangent map has at most one nonzero coefficient in its row. Invertibility forces the long block to be monomial, and the power relations force the branch permutation to preserve each \(d_i\). The annihilator of \(x_j\) times a unit in \(k[x_j]/(x_j^{d_j})\) is exactly \(k x_j^{d_j-1}\), which proves the unique off-principal terms. Conversely the displayed maps preserve all defining relations and have invertible cotangent map, so they are automorphisms. The finite-field formula counts the independent parameters in that normal form.

value.rationale: The mixed-length coordinate-cross algebra is a natural finite-dimensional family of fiber products of truncated one-variable branches. The theorem gives a complete normal form and exact finite-field order for every length vector, exposing the precise interaction between square-zero branches, longer branches of equal nilpotency index, and socle shears. This is a complete classification of a natural family, not an arbitrary parameter slice or a mere numerical recomputation.
